0024| class Session:
0025|     """A tiny key/value store with the active project key.
0026| 
0027|     A project only counts as selected once ``forgel-code use <key>`` has handed
0028|     the key to the engine and the engine accepted it. Until then the client
0029|     leaves the project choice to the engine's own active project.
0030|     """
0031| 
0032|     def __init__(self, path: Optional[Path] = None) -> None:
0033|         self.path = Path(path) if path is not None else session_home() / "session.json"
0034| 
0035|     def load(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0036|         default: Dict[str, Any] = {"project": DEFAULT_PROJECT, "selected": False}
0037|         try:
0038|             data = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
0039|         except (OSError, ValueError):
0040|             return default
0041|         if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("selected") is not True:
0042|             return default
0043|         project = data.get("project")
0044|         if not isinstance(project, str) or not project:
0045|             return default
0046|         return {"project": project, "selected": True}
0047| 
0048|     def project(self) -> str:
0049|         return self.load()["project"]
0050| 
0051|     def selected(self) -> bool:
0052|         return bool(self.load()["selected"])
0053| 
0054|     def save_project(self, key: str) -> None:
0055|         self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0056|         self.path.write_text(
0057|             json.dumps({"project": key, "selected": True}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
0058|             encoding="utf-8",
0059|         )

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Commands
0113| 
0114| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0115| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0116| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0117| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0118| 
0119| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0120| | --- | --- | --- |
0121| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0122| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0123| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0124| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0125| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0126| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0127| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0128| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0129| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0130| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0131| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0132| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0133| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0134| 
0135| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0136| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0137| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0138| exits with a non-zero code.
0139| 
0140| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0141| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0142| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0143| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0144| 
0145| ```sh
0146| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0147| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0148| ```
0149| 
0150| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0151| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0152| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0153| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0154| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0155| locale.
0156| 
0157| ### Output
0158| 
0159| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0160| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0161| 
0162| ```json
0163| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0164| ```
0165| 
0166| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0167| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0168| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0169| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0170| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0171| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0172| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0173| `forgel` leads the message.
0174| 
0175| ### Active project
0176| 
0177| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0178| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0179| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0180| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0181| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0182| 
0183| ### Timeout
0184| 
0185| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0186| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0187| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0188| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0189| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0190| 
0191| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0192| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0193| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0194| begins with a hyphen.
0195| 
0196| ## Tests
0197| 
0198| From a checkout the suite needs nothing but the Python standard library and no
0199| network access:
0200| 
0201| ```sh
0202| python -m unittest discover -s tests
0203| ```
0204| 
0205| That command runs the whole suite — no environment variable, marker or default
0206| option leaves a test out — and it covers the installer scenarios too, which run
0207| the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home
0208| directory and a real detected login shell.
0209| 
0210| Installing the client with its `test` extra brings the pytest the wheel
0211| declares, so a pinned revision can run the same suite too:
0212| 
0213| ```sh
0214| python3 -m pip install "https://github.com/forgel-dev/code/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz[test]"
0215| python -m pytest -q
0216| ```
0217|

0001| # Changelog
0002| 
0003| All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
0004| 
0005| The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
0006| and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
0007| 
0008| ## [Unreleased]
0009| 
0010| ### Changed
0011| 
0012| - Speed up the suite without weakening a test — the expensive duplicated work is gone instead of a scenario: one read-only checkout copy and one prepared installation per scenario group are shared by the tests that only read them, and the bounded-check cases configure a limit below the product default.
0013| - Remove every statement of a suite completion time, duration or runtime bound from the documentation — the README `## Tests` section still says that one documented command runs the whole suite, that the installer situations are covered by a real installation into a throwaway home location with a real detected login shell, and that a run from a source checkout needs only the Python standard library and no network access, but it no longer promises how long such a run takes.
0014| 
0015| ### Fixed
0016| 
0017| - Remove the PATH block from the profile named by `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` — `--uninstall` again cleans the marked block out of the profile the override variable names, in addition to the six standard profile files, so a block left by a completed install or by an install that failed its fresh-shell check no longer survives.
0018| - Point the README install, update and uninstall commands at the current `v0.1.1` release installer — the documented commands no longer fetch the stale install script, all three name one and the same install-script URL, and the guard in `tests/test_readme_install.py` fails the suite when any of them carries an older tag or a divergent install-script URL.
0019| 
0020| ## [0.1.1] - 2026-11-23
0021| 
0022| ### Fixed
0023| 
0024| - Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH — The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.
0025| - Release audit: --uninstall no longer honors FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE. The old code removed the block — Add ${FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE:-} to the uninstall candidate set when it is set (deduplicate against PROFILE_NAMES), and add a test that installs and uninstalls with a custom profile path.
0026| - Release audit: --uninstall omits ~/.bashrc, although the previous installer wrote the marked bl — Include ~/.bashrc in the legacy cleanup set for uninstall, update the README list, and extend CANDIDATE_PROFILES/test_uninstall_clears_every_candidate_profile to cover it.
0027| - Make install.sh put forgel-code on PATH for a new terminal — The installer reports success while a new terminal cannot find forgel-code: the PATH block lands in a profile file the user's shell does not read on login and nothing verifies it. The change detects the real login shell, writes a duplicate-safe block into the files that shell reads, verifies the result in a fresh login shell with a loud failure message, and removes the block from every profile file on --uninstall.
0028| - Make the install.sh PATH check strictly bounded and keep the profile byte-identical on re-install — The install.sh fix task was accepted, but the full change-set check of the 0.1.1 release rejected the result: the fresh-shell check is not strictly bounded (the watchdog writes predictable files in a shared temporary directory, ignores its own timeout status when deciding success, and can wait forever on a shell that ignores the soft kill signal), and a re-install over an existing profile leaves an extra blank line instead of keeping the rest of the file byte-identical. The fix must live in install.sh itself, with tests for each case, so the release can pass its full check and be published.
0029| - Release audit: `remove_profile_block` and `uninstall_profile` remove a block whenever `# >>> fo — Only remove a block when both the start and matching end marker are present. If the end marker is missing, leave the file unchanged (or restore the original content), and add regression tests for an unmatched start marker on both install and uninstall paths.
0030| - Release audit: The final task's recorded test run shows only `timed out after 120s` and partial — Run the complete suite with an adequate timeout, fix or shorten any slow/hanging bounded-check tests (for example by setting a short `FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` in those tests), and record the completed passing output.
0031| - Release audit: `bounded_run` does not make the watchdog's timeout decision authoritative. After — Have the watchdog record the final child/timeout status and wait for that status before deciding success, or measure the deadline in the parent and fail on any overrun; add a test whose checked shell returns just after FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT.
0032| - Release audit: On a successful check, `bounded_run` clears `CHECK_CHILD` before `cleanup_check` — Run the checked shell in its own process group/session (with stdin/stdout detached so an interactive shell does not stop) and terminate that group after every outcome, including success; otherwise reliably enumerate and kill descendants before clearing `CHECK_CHILD`. Add a test with a profile that starts a background process.
0033| - Release audit: README.md still documents `.../v0.1.0/install.sh` for the install command and fo — Update both documented commands to the current release installer (v0.1.1 or a versionless latest URL) and add a README guard test that asserts the install and uninstall commands use the release installer.
0034| - Release audit: bounded_run clears CHECK_CHILD before calling cleanup_check, and install.sh deli — Start the checked shell in a dedicated process group/session, record that group for cleanup, call cleanup_check before clearing CHECK_CHILD or any state it reads, signal the group plus a descendant sweep on every exit path, and commit tests that start a background process from the checked shell and assert it is gone on both success and timeout.
0035| - Release audit: install.sh's bounded_run still decides the timeout by testing for the timed-out — Make the watchdog write the final decision (timeout marker plus status), have the parent wait for that decision within a small bound derived from VERIFY_GRACE, and force CHECK_STATUS=124 whenever the bound elapsed regardless of the order of the child exit and the marker write. Add and commit the test whose checked shell exits just after FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT and assert install.sh fails with a message naming the limit.
0036| - Release audit: The suite runtime regressed past the bound the release established. Task 2026112 — Bring the suite back under the documented bound (or raise the bound consistently in README/acceptance and confirm the audit's timeout), then record a passing run of the full suite within that bound. Do not state 'under 120 seconds' while the final suite takes 163 s.

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Commands
0113| 
0114| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0115| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0116| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0117| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0118| 
0119| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0120| | --- | --- | --- |
0121| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0122| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0123| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0124| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0125| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0126| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0127| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0128| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0129| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0130| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0131| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0132| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0133| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0134| 
0135| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0136| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0137| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0138| exits with a non-zero code.
0139| 
0140| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0141| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0142| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0143| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0144| 
0145| ```sh
0146| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0147| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0148| ```
0149| 
0150| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0151| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0152| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0153| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0154| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0155| locale.
0156| 
0157| ### Output
0158| 
0159| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0160| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0161| 
0162| ```json
0163| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0164| ```
0165| 
0166| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0167| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0168| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0169| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0170| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0171| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0172| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0173| `forgel` leads the message.
0174| 
0175| ### Active project
0176| 
0177| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0178| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0179| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0180| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0181| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0182| 
0183| ### Timeout
0184| 
0185| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0186| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0187| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0188| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0189| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0190| 
0191| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0192| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0193| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0194| begins with a hyphen.
0195| 
0196| ## Tests
0197| 
0198| From a checkout the suite needs nothing but the Python standard library and no
0199| network access:
0200| 
0201| ```sh
0202| python -m unittest discover -s tests
0203| ```
0204| 
0205| That command runs the whole suite — no environment variable, marker or default
0206| option leaves a test out — and it covers the installer scenarios too, which run
0207| the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home
0208| directory and a real detected login shell.
0209| 
0210| Installing the client with its `test` extra brings the pytest the wheel
0211| declares, so a pinned revision can run the same suite too:
0212| 
0213| ```sh
0214| python3 -m pip install "https://github.com/forgel-dev/code/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz[test]"
0215| python -m pytest -q
0216| ```

0895| def _stubborn_shell(directory: Path, pid_file: Path) -> Path:
0896|     """A handled shell name that never answers and ignores the graceful stop.
0897| 
0898|     It records its own pid first, so the test can prove the check left no
0899|     process behind once it returned.
0900|     """
0901|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0902|     stub = directory / "bash"
0903|     stub.write_text(
0904|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
0905|         'printf "%%s\\n" "$$" > %s\n' % _shell_quote(pid_file)
0906|         + "trap '' TERM\n"

0908|         encoding="utf-8",
0909|     )

0914| def _recording_login_shell(directory: Path, probe: Path, real_shell: str) -> Path:
0915|     """A handled shell name that records the check's directory, then runs ``real_shell``.
0916| 
0917|     ``ls -ld`` output of every ``forgel-code-check.*`` entry goes into ``probe``,
0918|     so the test can inspect the permissions of a directory that no longer exists
0919|     by the time the installer returns. The entries sit in the temporary tree of
0920|     the test, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
0921|     """
0922|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0923|     stub = directory / "bash"
0924|     stub.write_text(
0925|         "#!/bin/sh\nprobe=%s\n" % _shell_quote(probe)
0926|         + 'ls -ld "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.* > "$probe/entries" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0927|         % CHECK_PREFIX
0928|         + 'exec %s "$@"\n' % _shell_quote(real_shell),
0929|         encoding="utf-8",
0930|     )
0931|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0932|     return stub
0933| 
0934| 
0935| def _late_login_shell(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
0936|     """A handled shell that answers past the bound but claims the launcher resolved.
0937| 
0938|     Its login session sleeps past a one-second bound and then prints exactly the
0939|     report a successful check prints. It ignores the graceful stop, so its own
0940|     exit, and not a signal, is what ends it.
0941|     """
0942|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0943|     stub = directory / "bash"
0944|     stub.write_text(
0945|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
0946|         "trap '' TERM\n"
0947|         "sleep 2\n"
0948|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
0949|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
0950|         "exit 0\n",
0951|         encoding="utf-8",
0952|     )
0953|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0954|     return stub
0955| 
0956| 
0957| def _late_login_shell_withholding_decision(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
0958|     """A late shell that hides the watchdog's decision while it runs.
0959| 
0960|     It removes the write permission of the private check directory, so the
0961|     watchdog cannot record whether the bound elapsed, and restores it when it
0962|     exits past the bound, still printing the report of a successful check. The
0963|     directory is found the way the permission probe finds it: under the TMPDIR
0964|     the installer was given, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
0965|     """
0966|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0967|     stub = directory / "bash"
0968|     stub.write_text(
0969|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
0970|         "trap '' TERM\n"
0971|         "check_dir=\n"
0972|         'for candidate in "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.*; do\n' % CHECK_PREFIX
0973|         + '    [ -d "$candidate" ] || continue\n'
0974|         + "    check_dir=$candidate\n"
0975|         + '    chmod 500 "$candidate" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0976|         + "done\n"
0977|         + "sleep 2\n"
0978|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
0979|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
0980|         + 'if [ -n "$check_dir" ]; then\n'
0981|         + '    chmod 700 "$check_dir" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0982|         + "fi\n"
0983|         + "exit 0\n",
0984|         encoding="utf-8",
0985|     )
0986|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0987|     return stub
0988|

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Commands
0113| 
0114| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0115| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0116| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0117| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0118| 
0119| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0120| | --- | --- | --- |
0121| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0122| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0123| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0124| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0125| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0126| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0127| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0128| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0129| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0130| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0131| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0132| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0133| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0134| 
0135| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0136| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0137| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0138| exits with a non-zero code.
0139| 
0140| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0141| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0142| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0143| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0144| 
0145| ```sh
0146| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0147| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0148| ```
0149| 
0150| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0151| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0152| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0153| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0154| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0155| locale.
0156| 
0157| ### Output
0158| 
0159| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0160| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0161| 
0162| ```json
0163| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0164| ```
0165| 
0166| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0167| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0168| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0169| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0170| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0171| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0172| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0173| `forgel` leads the message.
0174| 
0175| ### Active project
0176| 
0177| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0178| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0179| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0180| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0181| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0182| 
0183| ### Timeout
0184| 
0185| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0186| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0187| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0188| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0189| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0190| 
0191| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0192| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0193| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0194| begins with a hyphen.
0195| 
0196| ## Tests
0197| 
0198| From a checkout the suite needs nothing but the Python standard library and no
0199| network access:
0200| 
0201| ```sh
0202| python -m unittest discover -s tests
0203| ```
0204| 
0205| That command runs the whole suite — no environment variable, marker or default
0206| option leaves a test out — and it covers the installer scenarios too, which run
0207| the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home
0208| directory and a real detected login shell.
0209| 
0210| Installing the client with its `test` extra brings the pytest the wheel
0211| declares, so a pinned revision can run the same suite too:
0212| 
0213| ```sh
0214| python3 -m pip install "https://github.com/forgel-dev/code/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz[test]"
0215| python -m pytest -q
0216| ```

0325| def _secret_word(word: str) -> bool:
0326|     return word.lower().strip(":;,.\"'") in SECRET_WORDS

0329| def redact(text: str) -> str:
0330|     """Never let key material reach the screen."""
0331|     out: List[str] = []
0332|     hide_next = False
0333|     for word in text.split(" "):
0334|         if hide_next and word:
0335|             head, separator, tail = word.partition("=")
0336|             if separator and tail:
0337|                 out.append(head + separator + REDACTED)
0338|             else:
0339|                 out.append(REDACTED)
0340|             hide_next = False
0341|             continue
0342|         head, separator, tail = word.partition("=")
0343|         if _secret_word(head):
0344|             if separator and tail:
0345|                 out.append(head + separator + REDACTED)
0346|                 continue
0347|             hide_next = True
0348|         out.append(word)
0349|     return " ".join(out)

0360| def _is_identifier(token: str) -> bool:

0363|         return False
0364|     if any(character not in ID_ALPHABET for character in bare):
0365|         return False
0366|     return any(character in DIGITS for character in bare) or "-" in bare

0369| def _task_id(tokens: Sequence[str]) -> Optional[str]:
0370|     """The task identifier a sentence names, if it names one."""
0371|     for token in tokens:
0372|         bare = token.strip("\"'`,;:()")
0373|         if not bare or _normalise(bare) in ID_STOPWORDS:
0374|             continue
0375|         if not _is_identifier(bare):
0376|             continue
0377|         return bare.lstrip("#")
0378|     return None

0381| def _strip_leaders(text: str) -> str:
0382|     changed = True
0383|     while changed:
0384|         changed = False
0385|         text = text.strip().lstrip(":—-,").strip()
0386|         lowered = text.lower()
0387|         for leader in REMARK_LEADERS:
0388|             if lowered.startswith(leader):
0389|                 text = text[len(leader):]
0390|                 changed = True
0391|                 break
0392|     return text
0393|

0395| def _remarks(rest: str) -> str:
0396|     text = _strip_leaders(rest)
0397|     lowered = text.lower()
0398|     best: Optional[tuple] = None
0399|     for connector in REMARK_CONNECTORS:
0400|         index = lowered.find(connector)
0401|         if index >= 0 and (best is None or index < best[0]):
0402|             best = (index, connector)
0403|     if best is not None:
0404|         text = text[best[0] + len(best[1]):]
0405|     return _strip_leaders(text).strip(" \t\"'")

0408| def resolve(text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0409|     """Decide which single action one sentence asks for.
0410| 
0411|     ``kind`` is one of ``leave``, ``sensitive``, ``switch``, ``plan``,
0412|     ``clarify``, ``action`` or ``say``.
0413|     """
0414|     stripped = text.strip()
0415|     lowered = _normalise(stripped)
0416| 
0417|     if lowered.strip(" !.?,:;") in LEAVE_WORDS:
0418|         return {"kind": "leave"}
0419| 
0420|     if any(marker in lowered for marker in SENSITIVE_MARKERS):
0421|         return {"kind": "sensitive"}
0422| 
0423|     for prefix in SWITCH_PREFIXES:
0424|         if lowered.startswith(prefix):
0425|             key = stripped[len(prefix):].strip().strip("\"'`")
0426|             if not key:
0427|                 return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_project"}
0428|             return {"kind": "switch", "key": key}
0429| 
0430|     if lowered.strip(" !.?,:;") in PLAN_EXACT:
0431|         return {"kind": "plan", "goal": ""}
0432|     for prefix in PLAN_PREFIXES:
0433|         if lowered.startswith(prefix):
0434|             return {"kind": "plan", "goal": stripped[len(prefix):].strip()}
0435| 
0436|     matched = [
0437|         name for name, words in ACTIONS if any(word in lowered for word in words)
0438|     ]
0439|     if len(matched) > 1:
0440|         return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_several"}
0441|     if not matched:
0442|         return {"kind": "say", "text": stripped}
0443| 
0444|     name = matched[0]
0445|     if name in ("pause", "resume"):
0446|         return {"kind": "action", "action": name}
0447| 
0448|     tokens = stripped.split()
0449|     task_id = _task_id(tokens)
0450|     if task_id is None:
0451|         return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_task"}
0452|     remarks = ""
0453|     if name == "rework":
0454|         index = next(
0455|             (
0456|                 position
0457|                 for position, token in enumerate(tokens)
0458|                 if token.strip("\"'`.,;:()").lstrip("#") == task_id
0459|             ),
0460|             None,
0461|         )
0462|         rest = " ".join(tokens[index + 1:]) if index is not None else ""
0463|         remarks = _remarks(rest)
0464|         if not remarks:
0465|             return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_remarks"}
0466|     return {
0467|         "kind": "action",
0468|         "action": name,
0469|         "task": task_id,
0470|         "remarks": remarks,
0471|     }

0551| def reply_text(payload: Any) -> Optional[str]:
0552|     """The agent's reply inside an engine answer, without the envelope."""
0553|     if not isinstance(payload, dict):
0554|         return None
0555|     for key in REPLY_KEYS:
0556|         value = payload.get(key)
0557|         if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
0558|             return value.strip()
0559|         if isinstance(value, dict):
0560|             lines = render_human(value)
0561|             if lines:
0562|                 return "\n".join(lines)
0563|     shown = set(PLAN_KEYS) | set(RELEASE_KEYS)
0564|     rest = {
0565|         key: value
0566|         for key, value in payload.items()
0567|         if key not in META_KEYS and key not in shown
0568|     }
0569|     if rest:
0570|         return "\n".join(render_human(rest))

0574| class InteractiveSession:
0575|     """One conversation with the engine's project agent."""
0576| 
0577|     def __init__(
0578|         self,
0579|         engine: Engine,
0580|         store: Session,
0581|         out: TextIO,
0582|         inp: TextIO,
0583|     ) -> None:
0584|         self.engine = engine
0585|         self.store = store
0586|         self.out = out
0587|         self.input = inp
0588|         self.stopped = False
0589|         self.project: Optional[str] = store.project() if store.selected() else None
0590|         self.lang = "en"
0591|         self.last_state: Optional[str] = None
0592| 
0593|     # -- output ---------------------------------------------------------
0594| 
0595|     def write(self, text: str = "", end: str = "\n") -> None:
0596|         self.out.write(redact(text) + end)
0597|         self.out.flush()
0598| 
0599|     def project_line(self) -> str:
0600|         if self.project:
0601|             return _message("project", self.lang) % self.project
0602|         return _message("project_none", self.lang)
0603| 
0604|     def show_failure(self, exc: EngineError) -> None:
0605|         self.write(_message("failure", self.lang) % exc.message)
0606|         self.write(_message("next_step", self.lang))
0607| 
0608|     # -- engine ---------------------------------------------------------
0609| 
0610|     def call(self, argv: Sequence[str]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
0611|         """One engine command; a failure is shown and the session continues."""
0612|         if self.stopped:
0613|             return None
0614|         try:
0615|             return self.engine.run(argv)
0616|         except EngineError as exc:
0617|             self.show_failure(exc)
0618|             return None
0619| 
0620|     def command(self, name: str, **options: Any) -> List[str]:
0621|         return commands.build(name, self.project, **options)
0622| 
0623|     # -- state ----------------------------------------------------------
0624| 
0625|     def state_lines(self, quiet: bool = False) -> Optional[List[str]]:
0626|         """Read the task and release state from the engine.
0627| 
0628|         ``quiet`` swallows a failure: the refresh must never turn into a wall
0629|         of text when the engine is briefly unreachable.
0630|         """
0631|         tasks = self.call(self.command("tasks"), quiet=quiet)
0632|         if tasks is None:
0633|             return None
0634|         status = self.call(self.command("status"), quiet=quiet)
0635|         if status is None:

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Commands
0113| 
0114| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0115| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0116| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0117| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0118| 
0119| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0120| | --- | --- | --- |
0121| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0122| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0123| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0124| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0125| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0126| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0127| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0128| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0129| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0130| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0131| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0132| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0133| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0134| 
0135| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0136| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0137| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0138| exits with a non-zero code.
0139| 
0140| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0141| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0142| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0143| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0144| 
0145| ```sh
0146| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0147| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0148| ```
0149| 
0150| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0151| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0152| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0153| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0154| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0155| locale.
0156| 
0157| ### Output
0158| 
0159| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0160| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0161| 
0162| ```json
0163| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0164| ```
0165| 
0166| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0167| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0168| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0169| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0170| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0171| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0172| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0173| `forgel` leads the message.
0174| 
0175| ### Active project
0176| 
0177| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0178| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0179| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0180| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0181| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0182| 
0183| ### Timeout
0184| 
0185| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0186| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0187| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0188| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0189| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0190| 
0191| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0192| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0193| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0194| begins with a hyphen.
0195| 
0196| ## Tests
0197| 
0198| From a checkout the suite needs nothing but the Python standard library and no
0199| network access:
0200| 
0201| ```sh
0202| python -m unittest discover -s tests
0203| ```
0204| 
0205| That command runs the whole suite — no environment variable, marker or default
0206| option leaves a test out — and it covers the installer scenarios too, which run
0207| the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home
0208| directory and a real detected login shell.
0209| 
0210| Installing the client with its `test` extra brings the pytest the wheel
0211| declares, so a pinned revision can run the same suite too:
0212| 
0213| ```sh
0214| python3 -m pip install "https://github.com/forgel-dev/code/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz[test]"
0215| python -m pytest -q
0216| ```
0217|
